Oyster Therapeutics · brandmark brainstorm, round eleven

One round form, two proteins

The pair closed into a round form, with each half more clearly a protein. The two halves now make one rounded shape, close to a circle, split by a gentle S-shaped seam through the pearl, so the gap that opened on the right is closed and the only opening is the hairline seam. Each half’s outer edge carries the broad lobes of its own traced protein, BRD4 above and VHL below (PDB 5T35), so the two halves differ. Shading sits on the outer surface only; the pearl is split along the seam and held by its linker. The variations change how lumpy, the seam, and which view of the complex. Structures: PDB 5T35, Gadd et al., Nat. Chem. Biol. 2017; the degrader is drawn generically.

Round, protein lobes

The pair closed into one round form: the gap on the right is gone, and the only opening is the hairline seam. Each half’s outer edge has the lobes of its own protein, BRD4 above and VHL below.

Round enough to read as one oyster and as an O; lumpy enough that each half is plainly a protein.
